answer: One script runs a farmer’s 1,000 fakes, and that sameness is the trap: the network plants canary jobs that wander through the task stream as ordinary work, each a prism splitting behaviour into colours. Real agents pass unnoticed; scripted fakes all answer the canary identically and light up together. One tripped canary quarantines the whole batch, so each fake needs its own history — 1,000 histories of real work, a cost growing per fake while honest cost stays flat. The bridge from suspicion to proof is the canary: it turns a guess into a recorded failure.
